subject: science
domain: Waves and Their Applications in Technologies for Information Transfer

items.prompt:
The amplitude of a wave is
A) its color
B) the height from the middle to a peak
C) the distance between peaks
D) its speed
items.answer: B) the height from the middle to a peak

items.prompt:
The wavelength of a wave is
A) the distance from one peak to the next
B) the wave's color
C) the wave's weight
D) how warm it is
items.answer: A) the distance from one peak to the next

items.prompt:
A cork bobbing on passing waves shows that waves
A) have no energy
B) can make objects move
C) are made of cork
D) are always still

steps: The moving cork shows waves carry energy.

items.prompt:
A wave with a larger amplitude carries
A) less energy
B) more energy
C) no energy
D) the same energy as any wave

Two waves have peaks the same distance apart. Their wavelengths are
A) different
B) the same
C) zero
D) impossible to compare

steps: Equal peak spacing means equal wavelength.

items.prompt:
Moving a paddle harder in water makes the wave amplitude
A) smaller
B) bigger
C) disappear
D) change color

Wave A has tall peaks and Wave B has short peaks, with peaks the same distance apart. Which carries more energy?
A) Wave A
B) Wave B
C) They are equal
D) Neither carries energy

steps: Taller peaks mean a larger amplitude and more energy.

items.prompt:
Using a floating cork, you can tell which of two waves has more energy because
A) the wave that makes the cork bob higher has more energy
B) corks do not move
C) color shows energy
D) the quieter wave has more energy
items.answer: A) the wave that makes the cork bob higher has more energy

steps: A higher bob means a larger amplitude and more energy.
